name: market_profile_poc_5s
author: adapted from claude-4.6-opus-agent-3
thesis: Market Profile theory (developed by J. Peter Steidlmayer at CBOT) organizes price-time data into a distribution showing where volume was transacted. The Point of Control (POC) — the price level with the highest traded volume — acts as a magnet for price during range-bound days and as a launchpad during trend days. On 1-min Indian intraday charts, we compute the developing POC and Value Area (VA: price range containing 70% of volume) in real-time. When price deviates beyond the VA boundary but then fails to sustain the breakout, it reverts to POC. The inefficiency exists because: (1) Market Profile requires volume-at-price computation which standard charting platforms don't compute in real-time for Indian stocks, (2) the developing VA changes throughout the day, requiring dynamic recalculation, (3) most Indian traders use traditional support/resistance, not volume-based levels.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

indicators.name: POC
indicators.formula: price_level with max(volume_at_price) from session start to current bar

indicators.name: VA_high
indicators.formula: upper boundary of price range containing 70% of total session volume

indicators.name: VA_breakout_failed
indicators.formula: (close was > VA_high within last 5 bars AND close now < VA_high) OR (close was < VA_low AND close now > VA_low)

conditions: VA_breakout_failed == True (price broke below VA_low but came back)
POC_distance_bps < -10 (still below POC — room to revert up)
VA_breakout_failed == True (price broke above VA_high but came back)
POC_distance_bps > 10 (still above POC — room to revert down)

exit.signal_exit: POC shifts significantly (>10 bps) due to heavy volume at new price level

filters.vix_filter: India_VIX < 22 (Market Profile works best in range-bound markets)
filters.volume_filter: total session volume > 0.5x typical (sufficient data for profile)

weaknesses: Volume-at-price computation from OHLCV bars is an approximation — we distribute bar volume uniformly across the bar's range, which is inaccurate for bars with large wicks.
On trend days (estimated 20-30% of sessions), the Market Profile is one-directional with no reversion to POC. The strategy loses on trend days.
The developing POC and VA boundaries shift throughout the day, making the 'target' a moving target. A POC shift mid-trade can invalidate the exit level.
prior_art: Steidlmayer & Koy (1986) 'Markets and Market Logic' — original Market Profile. Dalton, Jones & Dalton (1990) 'Mind Over Markets'. In India, Market Profile is taught by traders like Bramesh (Bramesh Tech) and used by prop firms in Mumbai.
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; signal conversion from individual stock to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index; stop/target recalibration for 5-second timeframe. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
